London, 17<sup>th</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**The Canadian Auto Workers union** must make more concessions to ensure a proposed cooperation deal between Chrysler and Fiat goes through, Industry Minister Tony Clement said.  “With April 30 looming very closely on the horizon, the CAW has to do its part. ... This is not an easy thing, but the alternative is, there’s no deal in place, and if there’s no deal in place, there will not be long-term funding arrangements with the government of Canada, and in fact we have the right to call our loans.” _Source:  The Guardian_ 

**Chrysler** would cede control of its board and ultimately senior leadership if it completes a planned alliance with Fiat, Chrysler CEO Bob Nardelli said.  The U.S. government and Fiat would appoint a board of directors for Chrysler, with a majority of them independent directors who are not employees of either automaker, Nardelli said in an internal memo to workers. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Volkswagen** group may have passed Toyota as the world’s top selling automaker in Q109.  VW set a goal of overtaking Toyota and GM to be the world’s No.1 seller by 2018 -- a target that was initially met with skepticism.  But a deepening recession and credit crisis have hit demand in Toyota’s top markets, with U.S. sales falling 38% and Japan sliding 24% in Jan-March.  Volkswagen, meanwhile, is benefiting from government stimulus plans that have boosted sales in China, Germany and Brazil, which together accounted for 44%of group sales last year, making it more likely that it beat Toyota or at least came close.  Toyota has given no forecast for retail sales, but its latest estimate for shipments for the 2009 first quarter is 1.23 million vehicles, down 47 percent from a year earlier.  Volkswagen had projected a 10 percent decline in its global sales for 2009 back in January, but the sharp reversal in trends in Germany and China could alter that outcome. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**U.S. lawmakers** may let cars made overseas qualify for a proposed “cash-for-clunkers” program in a bid to secure passage of the measure.   An option under consideration would distribute subsidies to newcar buyers based on manufacturers’ U.S. market share, said Representative Betty Sutton, sponsor of the proposal. The approach may overcome objections that Sutton’s original plan subsidizes North Americanmade products only.   New autos sold at an annual rate of 9.86 million units in March, the slowest pace since 1982, according to Autodata Corp. The rate averaged 16.8 million this decade through 2007. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Brazil’s Companhia Vale do Rio Doce** will postpone the start-up of its Onca Puma nickel project, in Para state, by “at least one year”, and will halt nickel production in Sudbury, Ontario, for eight weeks in response to weak demand for the metal.  The Sudbury mining and processing operations will close from June 1 to July 27, following planned maintenance on th

e processing assets already scheduled for May. Spokesman Cory McPhee declined to comment on how much production would be affected by the shutdown, which will affect about 5 000 jobs.  He said that there are no plans at this point to extend the shutdown in Sudbury beyond the eight weeks. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Eastern Platinum** increased production at its Crocodile River mine (CRM) by 13%, marking record quarterly output and putting it on track to meet its full-year target. CRM produced 32,969 PGM for Q109. _Source:  Mining Mx_
